sourceChecks.text: The LORD spoke to Gad, David’s seer, saying,
sourceChecks.previousContext: David said to God, “I have sinned greatly, in that I have done this thing. But now put away, I beg you, the iniquity of your servant, for I have done very foolishly.”
sourceChecks.nextContext: “Go and speak to David, saying, ‘The LORD says, “I offer you three things. Choose one of them, that I may do it to you.”’”

sourceChecks.text: So Gad came to David and said to him, “The LORD says, ‘Take your choice:
sourceChecks.previousContext: “Go and speak to David, saying, ‘The LORD says, “I offer you three things. Choose one of them, that I may do it to you.”’”
sourceChecks.nextContext: either three years of famine; or three months to be consumed before your foes, while the sword of your enemies overtakes you; or else three days of the sword of the LORD, even pestilence in the land, and the LORD’s angel destroying throughout all the borders of Israel. Now therefore consider what answer I shall return to him who sent me.’”

sourceChecks.text: David said to Gad, “I am in distress. Let me fall, I pray, into the LORD’s hand, for his mercies are very great. Don’t let me fall into man’s hand.”
sourceChecks.previousContext: either three years of famine; or three months to be consumed before your foes, while the sword of your enemies overtakes you; or else three days of the sword of the LORD, even pestilence in the land, and the LORD’s angel destroying throughout all the borders of Israel. Now therefore consider what answer I shall return to him who sent me.’”
sourceChecks.nextContext: So the LORD sent a pestilence on Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fell.

sourceChecks.text: Then the LORD’s angel commanded Gad to tell David that David should go up and raise an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
sourceChecks.previousContext: David said to God, “Isn’t it I who commanded the people to be counted? It is even I who have sinned and done very wickedly; but these sheep, what have they done? Please let your hand, O LORD my God, be against me and against my father’s house; but not against your people, that they should be plagued.”
sourceChecks.nextContext: David went up at the saying of Gad, which he spoke in the LORD’s name.

sourceChecks.text: David went up at the saying of Gad, which he spoke in the LORD’s name.
sourceChecks.previousContext: Then the LORD’s angel commanded Gad to tell David that David should go up and raise an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.
sourceChecks.nextContext: Ornan turned back and saw the angel; and his four sons who were with him hid themselves. Now Ornan was threshing wheat.

sourceChecks.text: Now the acts of David the king, first and last, behold, they are written in the history of Samuel the seer, and in the history of Nathan the prophet, and in the history of Gad the seer,
sourceChecks.previousContext: He died at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor; and Solomon his son reigned in his place.
sourceChecks.nextContext: with all his reign and his might, and the events that involved him, Israel, and all the kingdoms of the lands.
